newsitem.title: USA: NY precious metals ends mixed, gold still nervous.
newsitem.headline: NY precious metals ends mixed, gold still nervous.

text.p: New York precious metals ended mixed with gold sliding in line with overnight losses as the market remained nervous, but palladium made good gains while silver was able to consolidate after last week's tumble.
The knock-on effect of Germany's plan, hatched last week, to reevalute Bundesbank gold reserves, reverberated Monday.

"I don't think Germany will sell any gold but so many people feel that if the rest of the European banks fudge their balance sheets, then there may be additional central bank gold sales," a bullion dealer said.
COMEX June gold ended $2.70 weaker at $342.20 an ounce.
Bullion was quoted at $341.30/$341.80 an ounce.
Floor sources said they were watching closely to see if bullion or spot gold dipped below the key psychological $340.00 an ounce level which could trigger strong selling across the futures contracts.
The markets were also awaiting the outcome of Tuesday's Federal Reserve's Open Market Committee which deliberates interest rates.
COMEX July silver halted Friday's slide and near the close was able to move higher on steadier note, ending 2.00 cents firmer at $4.713 an ounce, traded $4.72 to $4.62.5.
Gold and silver volumes were estimated at 37,000 and 12,000 lots respectively.
NYMEX June palladium ended $5.90 firmer at $178.00 an ounce, traded $178.10 to $169.25.
The market was still concerned about tightness in physical supply and the effect of any further glitches until Russia's 1997 export shipments begin, scheduled for mid-year, dealers said.
After being lower for much of the session, NYMEX July platinum ended unchanged at $391.20 an ounce, traded $392.90 to $385.50.

Monday, Johnson Matthey unveiled its Platinum 1997 report which indicated strong growth for palladium in auto catalysts, led by Ford in the U.S., and sharply rising offtake for platinum jewelry in China.
